claim: The abstract reports that, despite differences among settings, clinicians in all studied groups appeared to prioritize some types of tasks over others: documentation was generally given low priority in all groups, while the arrival of direct-care tasks tended to be treated with high priority. This is a qualitative descriptive tendency reported across three studies at one teaching hospital in Sydney, not an ED-specific priority assignment rule. The abstract does not provide a universal task ranking, decision-time eligible action set, urgency scale, thresholds, tie-break rule, or portable policy.

primary_source.units: Qualitative, group-level priority tendency (generally low priority for documentation; tendency toward high priority for incoming direct-care tasks). No priority scale or quantitative priority measure is reported.
